entities_included.other: Emory Healthcare (EHC: Emory Healthcare, Inc. and controlled operating companies incl. Emory University Hospital, Emory University Hospital Midtown, Emory Saint Joseph's Hospital, Emory Johns Creek, Emory Rehabilitation, DeKalb Medical, The Emory Clinic, Emory Specialty Associates, Wesley Woods, Clifton Casualty Insurance Co. captive, and Houston Healthcare System, Inc. acquired June 1, 2025) is included within the University (note 1, PDF p.9). Health-system expense: note 17 (PDF p.36) says 'the portion of patient care services related to Emory Healthcare expense is $7.6 billion' for FY25 ($6.7 billion for FY24, PDF p.37), stated only to the nearest $0.1 billion, hence 7,600,000,000. Cross-check: consolidated total operating expenses 10,577,959,000 less 'Emory University (excluding Emory Healthcare)' total operating expenses 2,996,817,000 (Schedule 2, PDF p.41) = 7,581,142,000. University-excluding-EHC salaries FY25 1,712,143,000 (FY24 1,582,886,000; FY23 1,438,433,000), so implied EHC salaries FY25 about 3,553,306,000 (derived by subtraction, before any intercompany eliminations). The Carter Center is a related party, not consolidated.

calibration_fy23.explanation: S&W matches exactly: reference 4,313,737,000 equals the FY23 'Salaries' line (fringe benefits of 935,867,000 are separate and excluded), 0.00% difference, consolidated including Emory Healthcare. Reference 'core operating expenses' 8,570,621,000 equals FY23 TOTAL operating expenses to the dollar; depreciation and amortization (359,420,000, combined line) and interest (92,896,000) were NOT removed. On the SPEC definition core opex FY23 = 8,570,621,000 - 359,420,000 - 92,896,000 = 8,118,305,000, which is 5.28% below the reference; the whole gap is D&A plus interest.

student_counts_in_official_docs: FY25 report note 1 (PDF p.9): 'Emory provides educational services to approximately 8,300 undergraduate students and 8,200 graduate and professional students within its nine schools and colleges.' (approximately 16,500 in total; the term is not stated).
caveats: FY25 is not fully comparable with FY24: Emory Healthcare acquired Houston Healthcare System (Perry and Warner Robins hospitals) on June 1, 2025, so about three months of it are in FY25; FY25 also had a depreciation-life study reducing depreciation by $27.1 million (note 10, PDF p.25) and FY24 interest is net of 17.5 million capitalized interest versus 0.0 in FY25.
Depreciation and amortization are a single combined operating line and cannot be split; the combined figure is subtracted as depreciation.
Interest on indebtedness includes the interest component of finance leases (lease note) and is a separate operating line, so it is fully inside operating expenses.
health_system_expense of 7.6 billion is a rounded figure stated in a note; the subtraction cross-check (7,581,142,000) supports it.
Operating expenses also include student financial aid (26,697,000 FY25), which is not part of salaries or benefits and stays in core opex.
